title: Dow Drops 325 Points as Tech Gets Crushed
text:
Text size
12:10 p.m. Uh oh. Here we go again.
The S&P 500 has dropped 1.3% to 2772.28, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has fallen 325.71 points, or 1.3%, to 25,380.97. The Nasdaq Composite has slumped 1.8% to 7507.06.
Like yesterday, the S&P 500 tried to battle back. But unlike yesterday, when that rally stalled out around the unchanged mark, selling started with a vengeance.
The S&P 500 Information Technology Sector index’s 1.9% drop makes it the worst performing sector, as Apple (AAPL) has slumped 2% to $216.78, and Microsoft (MSFT) has slid 2% to $108.46. The new S&P 500 Communication Services Sector index’s is also down 1.9%, as Facebook (FB) drops 2.7% to $155.12, and Netflix (NFLX) tumbles 4.6% to $3487.83.
MRA’s Mayank Seksaria notes that momentum is still getting clobbered , and that value’s outperformance—what there is of it—is not because investors suddenly like cheap stocks. The iShares Edge MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF (MTUM) has dropped 2% to 110.42, while the iShares Edge MSCI USA Value Factor ETF (VLUE) has fallen 1.4% to $83.75.
“The seeming rotation from Momentum to Value, is more likely a function of the fact that the Longs in the Momentum factor and shorts in the Value factor are highly correlated,” he explains.
With nothing to pick up the slack, this could get painful.
Write to Ben Levisohn at Close Dow Drops 325 Points as Tech Gets Crushed 12:10 p.
